newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court denies stay in NationsBank merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court denies stay in NationsBank merger.

text.p: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the tenth circuit Friday denied a stay requested by two community groups that would have temporarily blocked completion of the $9.8 billion acquisition by NationsBank Corp of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
The transaction is scheduled to be completed January 7.
One of the community groups said after learning of the denial that it was was considering seeking an emergency order from the U.S. Supreme Court.

"The arguments of all parties in support of and in opposition to the motion for stay have been carefully considered," the court's order said. "We conclude that petitioners have failed to show that they satisfy the tests for granting the relief sought. Accordingly, the motion for stay is denied."
The order was issued by a two-judge panel.
Matthew Lee, executive director of Inner City Press/Community on the Move, which has been opposing the merger, said the group was considering seeking an emergency order from the U.S. Supreme Court.

The order from the tenth circuit applied only to the request for a temporary stay blocking the closing of the merger until the court could decide the underlying issue of whether or not the Federal Reserve Board acted properly in approving the merger December 16.
Inner City Press, joined by the New Mexico Alliance, had argued that bank customers would be harmed by the merger.
The groups in particular alleged consumer finance units of Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank engaged in predatory loan practices. NationsBank strongly denied the allegation.

The community groups had also argued the approval process was flawed. The groups said that, during proceedings before the Federal Reserve, NationsBank failed to disclose planned branch closings. They also said lawsuits against the consumer finance units were not disclosed.
The Federal Reserve told the tenth circuit in a filing the groups lacked legal standing to challenge the approval.
Upon acquiring St. Louis-based Boatmen's, NationsBank would become the fourth-largest U.S. bank holding company with about $233 billion in assets.

As of September 30, 1995, NationsBank had $187.7 billion in assets and ranked fifth in size in the U.S. behind Chase Manhattan Corp, Citicorp, BankAmerica Corp and J.P. Morgan & Co. Boatmen's on that date was ranked twenty-fourth with $40.69 billion in assets.
After the merger, the combined bank will have 13 million customers in 16 states, 2,600 branches and 5,000 automated teller machines.
NationsBank shares closed up 1-1/4 at 98-5/8 Friday and Boatmen's rose 15/16 to 64-1/4.
